what: a king's crown made with a pair of bull's horns, with nobody wearing it: a broad band of yellow gold, a ring open at the top with only darkness inside it. what: an ancient Sumerian war helmet beaten from one sheet of gold in the shape of a head of hair, with nobody inside it: the round bowl is covered in bold wavy ridges like combed hair parted down the middle; a broad plain raised band runs round it like a headband; a round knot of golden hair sticks out at the back; and two rounded cheek guards hang down at the sides, each with a round boss where the ear would be. what: a tall Indian temple crown of gold with nobody wearing it: four round tiers stacked one on top of another, each tier narrower than the one below, so that the whole crown tapers like a tower; each tier is a band of gold edged with a row of upright lotus petals in gold, and each has one large round red ruby set in the middle of its front; on the very top sits a closed gold lotus bud. what: the god of the underworld's helmet of darkness, with nobody inside it: a plain ancient Greek helmet of dull black iron that covers the whole head in one smooth piece, with two almond-shaped eye openings, a straight nose guard between them and a narrow gap running down between two long cheek guards. what: a Spartan king's Corinthian helmet with nobody inside it: one smooth deep bowl of bronze covering the whole head, with two almond-shaped eye openings, a straight nose guard between them, and a narrow gap running down between two long pointed cheek guards. what: a Norse dragon-hoard helmet with nobody inside it: a plain round domed helmet of pale shining silver-white mithril, made of smooth plates joined by one riveted band round the brow and one over the crown, with one straight nose bar hanging down in front and two broad cheek guards. what: an Egyptian king's royal kilt with nobody wearing it: a knee-length wrap-around skirt of fine white linen pressed into many sharp upright pleats, hung from a broad stiff belt of gold at the waist. what: a kite shield carved from one great slab of clear pale blue crystal: a tall shield with a rounded top and long sides tapering to a sharp point at the bottom, twice as tall as it is wide, its face cut into large flat angular facets like a gemstone, with a bright white edge on every facet and one sharp ridge running down the middle from the top to the point. what: a plain common soldier's round wooden shield: a perfect circle made of six broad upright planks of dark oak butted side by side, with dark gaps between the planks, bold wood grain and a knot or two, held together by one small round domed iron boss in the very centre and four iron nail heads. what: a part taken from an ancient guardian machine: one thick round disc of dark gunmetal, like a heavy metal wheel hub lying face to the viewer, with six short square lugs of paler steel sticking out round its rim at even spaces, joined to it. what: a Thracian skirmisher's light wicker shield in the shape of a crescent. It is much wider than it is tall. what: an Aztec god's round shield, a perfect circle: the whole face is one disc of polished black volcanic glass, as glossy as a mirror, with two broad curved streaks of white reflected light across it and a dim grey sheen. Round it runs a broad rim made of small square tiles of bright turquoise stone set in a ring, and outside that a thin band of gold. There is nothing else on the face.
colours: Glossy jet-black glass with white and pale grey reflections; a bright turquoise tile rim; a thin yellow gold outer band.
pose: Seen from the front, upright, its face flat towards the viewer, the whole shield inside the picture.

what: the shield that stands in front of the sun: a round shield of bright gold. In its centre is a round domed boss of pale white-gold as bright as a flame. From the boss to the rim the face is embossed with twelve bold straight pointed rays, like the spokes of a wheel, each ray a long narrow triangle of paler gold with its point toward the rim. All round the edge of the shield stand twelve short broad triangular gold points, joined to the rim, so that the outline of the shield is spiky.
colours: Bright warm yellow gold, deep amber-gold between the rays, a pale white-gold centre.
pose: Seen from the front, upright, its face flat towards the viewer, the whole shield inside the picture.
must_show: bold rays from the centre to the rim

what: the goddess Athena's polished shield, the one lent to Perseus as a mirror: a large round shield, a perfect circle, gently domed, of pale silver-bronze polished until it shines like a mirror. The middle is completely smooth and blank and shows only reflected light: it is brightest white-gold in the centre and shades smoothly to deep warm bronze toward the rim, and across it, slanting from the upper left to the lower right, lie two broad straight streaks of pure white light, side by side, like sunlight on a window pane. Near the upper left sits one sharp glint of white light in the shape of a plus sign: one spike up, one down, one left, one right. Round the edge runs a broad raised rim of darker old bronze, as wide as a hand, set with twelve big round bright studs spaced evenly all round.
colours: Pale bright silver-bronze, white-gold in the middle and deep warm bronze-brown toward the rim, with pure white streaks of light; a darker old bronze rim with bright golden studs.
pose: Seen from the front, upright, its face flat towards the viewer, the whole shield inside the picture.
must_show: two slanting streaks of white light
broad dark bronze rim with round studs

what: the sacred shield of Rome that fell from the sky: an upright shield with a broad rounded top half and a broad rounded bottom half joined by a narrow waist, where one smooth round scoop curves into the left side and one into the right side. It is faced with one smooth sheet of polished bronze, bound all round its curving edge with a thick roll of dark red leather held by bronze studs, and across the narrow waist runs one bronze band with a round bronze boss in its middle.

must_show: one waisted bronze shield, narrow in the middle, rounded top and bottom
a round scoop in each side
band and boss at the waist

what: an ancient British river-offering shield of thin sheet bronze: a tall upright shield with straight sides and rounded ends, twice as tall as it is wide, a little narrower at the waist. On its face are three raised round panels in a column: a large one in the middle and a smaller one above it and below it, each filled with bold flowing raised curves. In the centre of the middle panel is a round domed boss, and set among the curves are many round studs of bright red glass, each as big as a cherry, about nine on the large panel and four on each small one.
colours: The shield is bright warm yellow-brown bronze like a polished brass door-knob, with dark brown shadows and no patina; the glass studs are bright blood red.

three round panels in a column, the middle one largest

what: a Norman horseman's long kite shield: a tall narrow shield with a fully rounded half-circle top and long sides that taper down to one long sharp point at the bottom, more than twice as tall as it is wide, like an almond standing on its tip. what: the war-aegis of Athena: a large round shield, a perfect circle, its face covered with bright silver scales in overlapping rows like the skin of a snake, shining pale and bright. In the very centre is the Gorgon's head as a round mask of dull bronze, a third of the shield wide: a broad flat face with wide round eyes, a wide mouth with tusks, and thick short snakes of dark green bronze curling out all round it like hair. All round the rim of the shield hangs a close fringe of short thick golden tassels, each joined to the rim and touching its neighbours, like the fringe of a rug.

bronze Gorgon mask with snake hair in the centre
fringe of gold tassels all round the rim

what: the Black Prince's shield for peace, a knight's heater shield: flat and straight across the top, with sides that curve inward to one point at the bottom, a little taller than it is wide. The face is flat black, with a thin rim of pale silver so the shape is lit. On the black stand three big white ostrich feathers, two side by side above and one below in the middle, each feather upright and plump with its tip curling over to one side and its white quill passing through a small pale scroll. Each feather is a third of the shield's height.

what: a Hittite chariot shield-bearer's shield: an upright shield with a broad rounded top half and a broad rounded bottom half joined by a narrow waist, where one smooth round scoop curves into the left side and one into the right side. what: a kite shield of the three Norns: a tall narrow shield with a rounded half-circle top and long sides tapering to a sharp point at the bottom, twice as tall as it is wide. what: a lost knight's battered steel shield, a heater shield: flat and straight across the top, with sides that curve inward to one point at the bottom, a little taller than it is wide, with a raised riveted rim. what: King Arthur's round shield Pridwen, a perfect circle, gently domed: the whole face is smooth shining white enamel, clean and bright. what: the death-god Yama's kite shield: a tall narrow shield of black iron with a rounded top and long sides tapering to a sharp point at the bottom, twice as tall as it is wide. what: an Assyrian archer's siege shield: a huge tall shield, twice as tall as it is wide, with a straight flat bottom edge, two straight upright sides, and a top that narrows to one blunt point. broad black iron strips across it

what: the shield of an ancient bronze giant: a huge tall flat rectangular shield, twice as tall as it is wide, with four sharp square corners, a straight top edge, a straight bottom edge and two straight parallel upright sides, like a tall door, a thick slab of bronze bound by a heavy raised rim with big rivets. The whole shield has turned dull green with age: a rough, crusty, dusty grey-green patina covers the face, darker in the hollows, and bare dark brown bronze shows on the raised rim, the rivets and the worn high spots. colours: Dull dusty grey-green verdigris, the colour of an old weathered copper roof, darker green in the hollows; dark brown bronze showing on the rim, rivets and the raised eye.

must_show: one very tall rectangular shield with square corners
dull grey-green with age all over
brown bronze showing on rim and rivets
one embossed eye in the centre

what: a Mycenaean tower shield of ox-hide, shown by itself: a huge tall flat rectangular shield, twice as tall as it is wide, with a gently arched top edge, a straight bottom edge and two straight parallel upright sides, like a tall door. A thick rim of dull bronze binds all the edges, lined with round rivets, and down the middle of the face, one above another, are three plain round bronze discs, each the size of a plate.

dark brown and cream ox-hide face
three bronze discs down the middle

what: the shield a god forged for the hero Aeneas: a huge tall shield, twice as tall as it is wide, a Roman rectangular shield with four square corners whose face bows outward like part of a great pipe. bright silver face with a broad gold border

what: a Roman legionary's shield, shown by itself: a huge tall flat rectangular shield, twice as tall as it is wide, with four sharp square corners, a straight top edge, a straight bottom edge and two straight parallel upright sides, like a tall door, its face bowed gently outward, bound round all four edges with a strip of brass. The whole face is painted deep red. In the very centre is a round domed iron boss on a square iron plate. Painted in bright gold, a pair of spread eagle's wings reaches out from the boss to the left and to the right, each wing as wide as a third of the shield; and one straight gold thunderbolt, a thick zigzag bar with an arrow point at its end, runs from the boss straight up, and another from the boss straight down. The gold thunderbolts stay inside the shield's edge.

gold wings spreading from the centre boss
gold thunderbolts above and below the boss

what: an ancient Greek hero's tower shield, shown by itself with nobody near it: a huge tall rectangular shield, twice as tall as it is wide, with a gently arched top edge, a straight bottom edge and two straight parallel upright sides, massive and thick like a slab of wall. The front is one sheet of dark old bronze hammered over layers of hide, covered in round hammer dents. In the very centre of it stands one big round domed boss of brighter bronze, a third as wide as the shield. Near the upper right corner is one deep black gash where a spear struck. All round the bronze, as a broad frame on all four sides, show the edges of the seven thick layers of dark bull's hide beneath it: a thick very dark brown border with pale lines between the layers, with a row of big round bronze rivets all the way round.
colours: The face is dark brown-gold bronze, the colour of tarnished brass, with deep brown shadows in the dents and warm golden highlights; the central boss is brighter golden bronze; the layered hide border is very dark brown with paler brown lines.
pose: Seen from the front, upright, its face flat towards the viewer, the whole shield inside the picture.

what: a penitent archbishop's hair shirt with nobody inside it: a rough long-sleeved undershirt that reaches the hips, woven of coarse dark goat hair in a bold open weave like sacking, bristling all over with short stiff hairs that stick out along every edge, with a plain round neck, and a length of knotted hemp cord tied round the waist with its two short ends hanging at the front.
